lines.japanese: 二限目の終わりに、教室の後ろのドアから、鞄を持った男子生徒が億劫そうに入ってきた。
lines.english: At the end of second period, a male student came trudging in through the rear door, schoolbag in hand.

lines.japanese: 遅れてきたのは明らかなのに、誰も彼のことを気に止めなかった。これがクラスの中でも存在感の高い……例えば渡来さんなら、みんなの意識が集中するのに。
lines.english: He was plainly late, yet no one paid him any mind. If he had been someone with more of a presence in the class—Watarai, for instance—every eye in the room would have turned.

lines.japanese: かと言って僕も話しかけられるほど親しいわけではないので、その遅れてきた年上の同級生に挨拶をすることは出来なかった。
lines.english: I was not close enough to him to strike up a conversation, though, so I could not bring myself to greet my older classmate when he came in.

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “’Sup.”

lines.japanese: そんな中、渡来さんが針生さんに顔を向けた。ほとんど唇を動かさずになにか一言告げたみたいだ。
lines.english: Across the room, Watarai turned to Hariu. Her lips barely moved; she seemed to murmur a single word to him.
“Hmph...”

lines.japanese: 二人の視線が合うと、目を閉じた針生さんの口端が少しだけ吊りあがって見えた。渡来さんもほとんど同時に、その端麗な顔立ちをほころばせる。
lines.english: Their eyes met. Hariu closed his, and one corner of his mouth seemed to lift by the slightest degree. At almost the same instant, Watarai's fine features softened into a smile.

lines.japanese: 一瞬のうちに、親交の深い者同士特有の、ほとんど無言の挨拶を交わしていた。
lines.english: In the space of a heartbeat, they had exchanged the nearly wordless greeting peculiar to close friends.

lines.japanese: そういえば昨日の朝、針生さんは渡来さんのことを下の名前で呼んでいた。仲がいいのかな。僕の知らないような場所で。
lines.english: Come to think of it, yesterday morning Hariu had called Watarai by her first name. Were they close? Somewhere I knew nothing about?

lines.japanese: 僕は渡来さんから目を逸らして、どこか違う場所へ泳がせてしまった。ベクトルを失った視線が、行き先もないままふらふらと漂う。
lines.english: I tore my eyes from Watarai and sent them swimming off in some other direction. Its vector gone, my gaze drifted aimlessly around the room.

lines.japanese: 行き着いたのは、５００ミリサイズのミネラルウォーターだった。針生さんは喉が渇いたのか、逆さにしたペットボトルからごっごっと水を流しこんでいく。
lines.english: It came to rest on a five-hundred-milliliter bottle of mineral water. Perhaps Hariu was thirsty: he tipped up the plastic bottle and gulped the water down.

lines.japanese: そのとき不意に彼の視線とぶつかった。偶然かなと思ったけど、キャップをしながらそれを鞄に収める間も、何度か目が合った。
lines.english: Then, without warning, his gaze collided with mine. I thought it might be chance, but our eyes met several more times as he capped the bottle and put it away in his bag.

lines.japanese: 向こうも気づいているはずなのに、彼からのアクションは何もない。居たたまれなくなった僕は、思いきって声をかけてみることにした。
lines.english: He had to know I was looking, yet he made no move at all. Unable to bear the awkwardness any longer, I screwed up my courage and spoke to him.

lines.japanese: 「あの、針生さん」
lines.english: “Um, Hariu?”

lines.japanese: クラス中の視線が僕に集まった気がする。僕の行動なんて誰も気に止めないと思うけど、もしかしたら針生さんが誰かと話すことは珍しいから、注目されてるのかもしれない。
lines.english: I felt every eye in the class turn toward me. Ordinarily no one would take any notice of what I did, but perhaps the spectacle of Hariu speaking to someone was rare enough to draw attention.

lines.japanese: 針生さんの三白眼が、突きあげるように僕へ向けられた。だけど口はむっつりと閉じたままで、僕は次の言葉を出さないわけにはいかなかった。
lines.english: Hariu looked sharply up at me, whites showing beneath his irises. His mouth remained clamped firmly shut, however, and I had no choice but to offer another line.

lines.japanese: 「今日はどうして遅れてきたんですか？」
lines.english: “Why were you late today?”

lines.japanese: 二度目の問いかけにも彼は答えなかった。背を後ろにそり返したため、ぎしっと椅子のきしむ音がした。
lines.english: He did not answer my second question either. He leaned back, and his chair gave a protesting creak.

lines.japanese: 僕は三度目の問いかけを繰りだした。
lines.english: I launched a third attempt.

lines.japanese: 「もしかしてまだ覚えてもらってませんか。学級委員の羽田鷹志です」
lines.english: “Do you still not remember me? I'm Takashi Haneda, the class rep.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ──」
lines.english: “You—”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの口が微かに動いて、低い声が聞こえてきた。
lines.english: Hariu's lips moved faintly, and a low voice reached me.

lines.japanese: 「──なかなかに鬱陶しいやつだな」
lines.english: “You’re quite the nuisance.”

lines.japanese: それは低い声のわりに、教室の空気を裂いて僕の耳へ入ってきた。
lines.english: Low as it was, his voice sliced through the classroom air and reached me with perfect clarity.

lines.japanese: そして、それきり針生さんは微々とした笑みを浮かべて黙りこんでしまった。
lines.english: And with that, Hariu sank back into silence, the barest trace of a smile on his lips.

lines.japanese: 「というわけで、いま黒板に書きだした仕事を分担したいのですが――」
lines.english: “So, as I was saying, I'd like to divide up the jobs I've written on the board—”

lines.japanese: 「委員長ー、早くしないと昼メシ食えなくなっちゃうでしょー？」
lines.english: “Class rep, hurry it up or we won't have time to eat lunch!”

lines.japanese: 「ッぞウゼーなあ……決めンならとっとと決めて、はやく終わらせてくんねー？」
lines.english: “God, this is such a pain... If we're gonna decide, let's just decide already and get it over with, okay?”

lines.japanese: 昼休みが始まってから２０分経過。会議は進んでいなかった。
lines.english: Twenty minutes had passed since lunch break began. The meeting had gotten nowhere.

lines.japanese: 教壇に立つ僕の隣りには、副委員長の高内さんが足を組んで座っている。その片側の足で、さっきから何度か床をこつこつ叩いていた。まだ彼女は一言も発していない。
lines.english: Beside me at the teacher's platform sat Takauchi, the deputy class rep, one leg crossed over the other. For some time now, she had been tapping one foot against the floor. She had yet to say a word.

lines.japanese: でもそれは仕方ないんだ。彼女はみんなを集めるところまでやってくれた。それなのに、自ら議事進行を買ってでた僕のせいで、話がまるでまとまっていないんだから。そう、それだ。
lines.english: But I could hardly blame her. She had done her part and gathered everyone here. I was the one who had volunteered to conduct the meeting, and thanks to me the discussion showed no sign of coming together. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「この、写真をまとめる係、これをやってくれる人はいませんか」
lines.english: “Is there anyone willing to take charge of sorting the photographs?”

lines.japanese: 誰も手を上げない。そもそも誰が好きこのんで、この忙しい時期にそんな役割を受けもってくれると言うんだろう。
lines.english: Not a hand went up. Why would anyone willingly take on a job like that at this busy time of year?

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ推薦でもいいので、誰か――」
lines.english: “Then a nomination would be fine. Does anyone—”

lines.japanese: それすら誰も手を上げなかった。ケータイをいじる男子、雑談に興じている女子、話を聞こうという生徒はひとりもいない。
lines.english: Still not a hand. Boys toyed with their phones, girls carried on their conversations; not one student was listening.

lines.japanese: ここにみんなを集めたのは副委員長の高内さん。なのに正委員長の僕は、話を聞いてもらうことすら出来ない。仕方がないので、こちらから指名することにした。
lines.english: Takauchi, the deputy class rep, had managed to assemble them all. I, the actual class rep, could not even persuade them to listen. There was nothing for it. I would have to call on someone myself.

lines.japanese: 「ええと、岡村さん。誰か推薦できる人はいませんか」
lines.english: “Um, Okamura. Is there anyone you'd like to nominate?”

lines.japanese: 「えッ！　私！？　なんで私に聞くん？」
lines.english: “What! Me!? Why are you asking me?”

lines.japanese: 「あの、誰かに聞かないと話が進まないし……」
lines.english: “Well, we won't get anywhere unless I ask somebody...”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんでそれで私が狙い撃ちされてんの！？　何ソレ、何かワケわかんないんだけど、どゆこと！？」
lines.english: “Huh? How does that mean I’m the one getting singled out!? What is that? I don’t even get it—what’s going on!?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、狙い撃ちとかじゃなくて、誰かに聞いてみようと思って……」
lines.english: “I didn't mean to single you out. I just thought I'd try asking someone...”

lines.japanese: 「んじゃ何で私なんだよ！　おかしいでしょ？」
lines.english: “Then why'd it have to be me? That's messed up!”

lines.japanese: 「はーい！」
lines.english: “Ooh, me!”

lines.japanese: 指名した女子の代わりに、彼女と話していた友人が手を上げてくれた。
lines.english: The friend she had been talking with raised a hand in her place.

lines.japanese: 「羽田クンにお願いしたいと思いまーす！」
lines.english: “I nominate Haneda!”

lines.japanese: どっと笑いが起こった。さっき指した女の子が友人の肩をばしばしと叩いている。
lines.english: The class erupted in laughter. The girl I had called on smacked her friend repeatedly on the shoulder.

lines.japanese: 「おれは他の仕事があるから無理だよ。誰か他の人にお願いしたいんだ」
lines.english: “I can't. I have other work to do. I need somebody else to take it.”

lines.japanese: だけど僕の声は、クラスメイトの笑い声に飲まれて消えた。困った、このままじゃ一人も決まらないで昼休みが終わってしまう。
lines.english: But my voice vanished beneath my classmates' laughter. This was bad. At this rate, lunch break would end before we assigned a single person.

lines.japanese: 隣りでこつこつの音が止んで、高内さんが立ちあがった。
lines.english: Beside me, the steady tapping stopped. Takauchi rose to her feet.

lines.japanese: 「あーも、いつまでたっても進まねーなあ。あのさ、委員長。うちら昼休みの時間貴重なんだけど、その辺分かってんの？」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. We're never gonna get anywhere at this rate. Listen, class rep—our lunch break is precious, you know? Do you even get that?”

lines.japanese: 分かってる。僕だって早く昼食をとりたいと思ってる。
lines.english: I did. I wanted to eat my lunch as soon as possible too.

lines.japanese: もしかして彼女は僕が食事をしない生き物だとでも思ってるんだろうか。同じ人間だ、誰だって昼休みは惜しいんだ。
lines.english: Did she imagine I was some species of creature that did not require food? We were both human. Lunch break was precious to everyone.

lines.japanese: ――いや、だからこそ高内さんはこうして会議を早く終わらせようとしてるんだ。少し言い方がきついだけで、言ってることは彼女の方が正しいじゃないか。
lines.english: —No. That was precisely why Takauchi was trying to bring the meeting to a quick conclusion. Her manner was a little harsh, but she was the one in the right.

lines.japanese: 「そうだね、高内さんの言うとおりだよ。だから誰かに推薦してもらおうと思ったんだ」
lines.english: “You're right, Takauchi. That's why I thought we could have people nominate someone.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、それでさっきから決まらないんだっつってンの！　臨機応変に対処しろよ、使えねーな！」
lines.english: “And that's why we've been getting nowhere! Use your head and adapt, for God's sake. You're useless!”

lines.japanese: 臨機応変。いい言葉だなと感心した。
lines.english: Adaptability. What a fine word, I thought admiringly.

lines.japanese: 「んじゃさー、仕事分けんのグループごとにすればいーじゃん、班分けしよーよ。それなら一人に押しつけることンなんないし、動きやすいっしょ」
lines.english: “Okay, then—why don't we split the work up by group? Let's split into groups. That way it doesn't all get dumped on one person, and it'll be easier to get things done.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、うん！　そうしよう！」
lines.english: “Oh—yes! Let's do that!”

lines.japanese: 僕は高内さんの閃きに感動した。臨機応変。こういうことだ。
lines.english: I was deeply impressed by Takauchi's flash of inspiration. Adaptability. This was what it meant.

lines.japanese: 「んじゃ、今から四人ずつの班決め開始ー。割りきれる人数だし、ちょうどよくね？」
lines.english: “Okay, everybody, groups of four. We divide evenly, so that works out perfectly, right?”

lines.japanese: がたがたと椅子が動いて、それぞれが後ろを向いたり、今まで話していた相手とうなずきあったり。会議は一気に進展をみせた。
lines.english: Chairs clattered. People turned around, exchanged nods with the friends they had already been talking to. In an instant, the meeting sprang to life.

lines.japanese: 高内さんはいつもの友人たちに声をかけていた。そうだ、僕も早く班決めをしないと。でないと会議を遅らせることになる。
lines.english: Takauchi was calling out to her usual friends. Of course—I needed to find a group quickly too, or I would be the one holding up the meeting.

lines.japanese: だけど僕には、声をかける相手が見つからなかった。僕のたった一人の友人だった森里君は、もうこのクラスにいない。
lines.english: But I could find no one to ask. Morisato, the only friend I had, was no longer in this class.

lines.japanese: いつだったか遠足の班決めしたときのことを思い出した。あのときは結局最後まで決まらなくて、一人足りないグループに入れてもらったんだ。
lines.english: I remembered picking groups for a field trip once. That time, I still didn’t have a group at the very end, so they put me in one that was short a person.

lines.japanese: そんなことを思いだしながら突ったっていると、高内さんが教壇へ戻ってきた。その表情には明らかにいらついた色が見える。彼女は僕に詰めよってきた。
lines.english: As I stood there remembering, Takauchi returned to the teacher's platform. The irritation on her face was unmistakable. She marched straight up to me.

lines.japanese: 「何やってんのおまえ？」
lines.english: “What the hell are you doing?”

lines.japanese: なにをしているんだろう。僕にも自分が何をしているのか分からない。臨機応変。僕は頭の中で繰りかえした。
lines.english: What was I doing? I did not know myself. Adaptability, I repeated inside my head.

lines.japanese: 「あのさあ、あんたが早く決めないといつまでたっても終わらないんだけど」
lines.english: “Listen, unless you hurry up and pick, we're never going to finish.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね、ええとまだ空いてるひとっているかな」
lines.english: “You're right. Um... is there anyone who still has room?”

lines.japanese: 「なんで私に聞くんだよ、自分で相手くらい探せッつーの」
lines.english: “Why're you asking me? Find somebody yourself, for crying out loud.”

lines.japanese: もう班分けが決まったクラスメイトたちは教壇に立つ僕を見て笑っていた。
lines.english: My classmates, already secure in their groups, looked up at me on the platform and laughed.

lines.japanese: 僕のせいで会議が進まないんだ、高内さんが怒るのも仕方ない。彼女は黙っている僕を見て、足をこつこつ鳴らし始めた。
lines.english: I was the reason the meeting could not move on. Takauchi had every right to be angry. She watched me stand there in silence and began tapping her foot again.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと、聞いてんの？　シカトこいてンじゃねーよ、大体あんたさあ――」
lines.english: “Hey, are you even listening? Don't just stand there ignoring me. You know, you've got this whole—”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　羽田班の枠、まだ空いてんの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Is there still room in Haneda's group?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんが一歩近づいたとき、よく通る声が僕と彼女の間を抜けていった。
lines.english: Just as Takauchi stepped closer, a clear voice passed cleanly through the space between us.

lines.japanese: 教壇近くの流れるように長い髪がふわっと僕の方へ向いた。渡来さんだ。彼女は友人たちに片手を立てて謝ると、さらにその手を高く掲げて宣言した。
lines.english: Near the platform, a long sweep of flowing hair turned lightly toward me. It was Watarai. She raised one hand in apology to her friends, then lifted it higher and made her declaration.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ私、羽田班いきまーす」
lines.english: “Then I'm joining Team Hanedaaa.”

lines.japanese: その声は雑然とした教室内によく響いた。
lines.english: Her voice carried clearly through the disorder of the classroom.

lines.japanese: 高内さんは口を開けたまま渡来さんの手を見ていた。もっとも、それより間抜けた顔をしていたのは僕だったんだろうけど。
lines.english: Takauchi stared openmouthed at Watarai's raised hand. Though I suspect my own face looked even more idiotic.

lines.japanese: 「え、なにその顔、もしかして駄目だった？」
lines.english: “What's that face for? Was I not allowed?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「駄目なんだ」
lines.english: “So I'm not.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなわけないよ。じゃあ一緒に組もう。お願いします」
lines.english: “No, of course not. Let's be in the same group. I'd be glad to have you.”

lines.japanese: 「よろしくね」
lines.english: “Likewise.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは爽やかすぎる微笑みをひとつ浮かべた。同時にどこかから舌打ちが聞こえた。だけどその音はあまり気にならなかった。
lines.english: Watarai gave me a smile almost too radiant to bear. At the same moment, someone clicked their tongue nearby. Somehow, the sound did not trouble me very much.

lines.japanese: ふと見渡すと、他の男子も一様に僕の顔を見ていた。なんていうか、今までに向けられたことのない種類の顔。羨望というか、嫉妬というか、そもそも初めて見るんだから判別しようがない。
lines.english: I glanced around and found the other boys staring at me too. Their faces wore expressions I had never seen directed my way before. Envy, perhaps, or jealousy—I had never encountered either one, so how was I to tell?

lines.japanese: こういうときに、自分がどういう顔をしていいか分からなかったから、とりあえず下を向いてやりすごすことにした。これも初めての体験だ。臨機応変。いい言葉だなと思った。
lines.english: I had no idea what expression I ought to wear in return, so I lowered my head and waited for the moment to pass. Another first. Adaptability. What a fine word.

lines.japanese: だけど、結局班決めが最後まで終わらなかったのは、やっぱり僕だった。
lines.english: But sure enough, I was the one who still didn’t have a group until the very end.

lines.japanese: 現在の班員は、僕、それと渡来さん。半分しか決まってない。
lines.english: So far, our group was me and Watarai. We were only halfway done.

lines.japanese: 「んでェー、あと決まってないの誰よ」
lines.english: “All right, who's still left?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは黒板に書きだされた決定済みの名前を見ながら、出席簿と照らしあわせた。
lines.english: Takauchi compared the roster against the names already written on the board.

lines.japanese: 「あと決まってないのってー、今日休んでる山科と……ハリウッドのおっさん？」
lines.english: “That leaves Yamashina, who’s absent today… and the Hollywood geezer?”

lines.japanese: 教室内の声が一瞬止まった。高内さんはあだ名で呼んだけど、彼の名前は教室内を静めさせる不思議な迫力がある。
lines.english: The classroom went quiet for a second. Takauchi used his nickname, but even that had some weird power to silence the room.

lines.japanese: その当人はまぶたを半開きにしたまま、背中をぎしりと椅子へ寄りかけていた。
lines.english: The man himself remained tipped back in his creaking chair, eyelids half lowered.

lines.japanese: 「おーい、おっさん。聞いてんの？　いまあんたのこと話してんだけど、形だけでもいいからどっか入ってよ」
lines.english: “Hey, old man. You listening? We're talking about you here. It can be in name only—just join one of the groups.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはそれでもしばらく黙っていたけど、やがて目を逸らし、体を前へ傾けながら口を開いた。
lines.english: Hariu stayed quiet a little longer, then looked away, leaned forward, and spoke.

lines.japanese: 「めんどくせえな」
lines.english: “What a pain in the ass.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「形だけでいいのなら、空いてるところに放り込めばいいでしょう。俺の意思を確認する必要があるのかい？」
lines.english: “If my name is all you need, put me wherever there's room. Is there any reason to consult my wishes?”

lines.japanese: 温度の低い教室内で針生さんの声はよく響いた。威圧的な口調でもないのに、押さえつけられるように空気が肩へ圧しかかる。
lines.english: Hariu's voice carried well in the chilly classroom. There was nothing openly threatening in his manner, yet the air seemed to bear down upon my shoulders.

lines.japanese: 会話の上手な人は「間」を上手く使えると聞いたことがある。これも針生さんが作りだす「間」なんだろうか。
lines.english: I had heard that gifted conversationalists knew how to make good use of silence. Was this another silence of Hariu's making?

lines.japanese: 「……はぁ。まあ、あんたがそれでいいッてんなら、別にいいけどォー」
lines.english: “...Fine. If that's what you want, I guess I don't care.”

lines.japanese: やがて高内さんが吐きすてるように言った。他には誰も声をあげない。
lines.english: After a while, Takauchi spat out the words. No one else spoke.

lines.japanese: 「んじゃさ、あと休んでる山科も入れて羽田班決まりでいいでしょ？　で、どうすんの委員長」
lines.english: “Then we'll put you and the absent Yamashina in Haneda's group. Settled, right? So what now, class rep?”

lines.japanese: 「え、どうするってなにを？」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what now?”

lines.japanese: 「なにをじゃねーよ、さっさと進めろよ。あんたが自分で議事進行するって言ったんじゃん。最初から最後まで、全部私に任せるつもりかよ」
lines.english: “Don't give me that. Get on with it. You're the one who said you'd run this meeting. Were you planning to dump the whole thing on me from beginning to end?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、いや……ええと、じゃあこれから役割の分担を……」
lines.english: “Oh. No, I... Um, now we'll divide up the responsibilities...”

lines.japanese: 「はァ！？　だから時間ないんだっつってんだろ！　元々あんたが引きうけたんだから、決まらなかった分の仕事はあんたの班で受けもってよ」
lines.english: “What!? I told you we're out of time! You volunteered for this in the first place, so your group can take whatever jobs haven't been assigned.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、それは無理だよ」
lines.english: “What? We can't do that.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ多数決取る？　いまの私の意見に賛成のひと――」
lines.english: “Then shall we vote? Everyone in favor of my proposal—”

lines.japanese: 結果は見るまでもなかった。僕のまるで知らないところで進められていくクラス会議。
lines.english: I didn’t need to watch the result. The class meeting went on without me knowing what was happening at all.

lines.japanese: この会議は、誰のために行われているんだろう。僕は自ら意識を眠らせて、幾つも上がったクラスメイトの腕を数えた。呼吸器官が苦しかった。
lines.english: For whose benefit was this meeting being held? I put my awareness deliberately to sleep and counted the arms rising around the classroom. My breathing apparatus was in distress.

lines.japanese: 「きゃはは、やるじゃん羽田。私あんたのこと見直しちゃったあ。そんで、あとはいつから始めるかだけどー」
lines.english: “Ahaha, look at you, Haneda! I'm starting to see you in a whole new light. Now all we have to decide is when to start.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……そうだね」
lines.english: “Yeah... I guess so.”

lines.japanese: 息がしづらくて声が出しにくかった。僕はこの会議を終わらせる言葉を探していた。先生みたいに言えばいいんだろうか。
lines.english: It was hard to breathe, which made it hard to speak. I looked for something that would end the meeting. Should I say it like a teacher?

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、明日から作業を始めるので、手伝ってくれる人は放課後、この教室に残ってください」
lines.english: “We'll begin tomorrow. Anyone willing to help, please remain in this classroom after school.”

lines.japanese: そんなことを言った気がするけど、本当に誰かが来るなんて期待はしなかった。放課後という自由時間までも学校に縛られたくないのは、僕もみんなも同じはずだから。
lines.english: I think I said something like that, but I didn’t actually expect anyone to come. None of us wanted school taking up our free time after classes too.

lines.japanese: 長かった会議は終わって、みんなが体を伸ばしたり、雑談を再開したり、教室中の空気は柔らかいものになった。
lines.english: The long meeting ended. People stretched, conversations resumed, and the air throughout the classroom turned soft again.

lines.japanese: 昼休みの残り時間が少ないので、昼食を慌てて食べる羽目になった。いくつかのパンを取りだして口の中へ詰めこむ。
lines.english: There was little left of lunch break, so I had to hurry through my meal. I took out several pieces of bread and stuffed them into my mouth.

lines.japanese: もちろん会議が遅れたのは僕のせいだから、自業自得と言えばそれまでだ。
lines.english: Of course, the meeting had run long because of me. I had brought this upon myself, and there was no more to be said.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ、なんでこんな慌てて弁当食べなきゃいけないわけェ？　弁当も味が分からなくなるっつのー」
lines.english: “Ughhh, why do I have to wolf down my lunch like this? You can’t even taste it when you eat this faaaast.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんの声が聞こえた。これは僕が会議を遅らせたんだから仕方ない。彼女は友人たちになだめられながら、まだ不平を口にしていた。
lines.english: Takauchi's voice reached me. I could hardly complain; I was the reason the meeting had run over. Her friends tried to soothe her, but her grievances continued.

lines.japanese: 「はあーあ、お茶もろくに買ってこらんないしさあ。ッたく、羽田に買って来てほしいよねえー」
lines.english: “Ugggh, I didn’t even have time to get any tea. Jeez, it’d sure be nice if Haneda went and bought me some, huh?”

lines.japanese: 彼女の声は教室の隅まで聞こえるような音量だった。がん、と机の脚を蹴る音。ああそうだ、僕が悪いんだから、お茶くらいは買ってきてあげるべきかもしれない。
lines.english: Her voice was loud enough to reach every corner of the room. Bang—a kick against a desk leg. Oh, right. This was my fault. Maybe I should at least go buy her some tea.

lines.japanese: そういえば、僕も飲み物を用意してなかったじゃないか。だからそのついでに彼女の分も買ってきてあげればいい。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I had no drink of my own. I could buy hers while I was there.

lines.japanese: 僕は机の脇にかけてあった鞄から財布を取りだすと、残りのパンを口に突っこんで立ちあがった。喉がからからに渇いていて、すぐに詰まった。
lines.english: I took my wallet from the bag hanging beside my desk, crammed the rest of the bread into my mouth, and stood. My throat was parched. The bread lodged in it at once.

lines.japanese: 「かふ、こふこふっ」
lines.english: “Kh—koff, koff!”

lines.japanese: 少し咽ると食べたばかりの卵パンが口から漏れた。隣の席の女子が汚いなあと言って机から離れていった。僕は口元を軽くこすった。
lines.english: I choked a little, and some of the egg-filled bread I’d just eaten came out of my mouth. The girl at the desk next to me said, ‘Gross,’ and moved away. I wiped my mouth.

lines.japanese: こんなことをしている場合じゃないんだ。高内さんの飲み物を買ってきてあげないと。だけど、焦ってもでてくるのは咳ばかりで、足はちっとも前へ動こうとしなかった。
lines.english: This wasn’t the time for this. I had to go buy Takauchi a drink. But when I tried to hurry, all that came out was coughing, and my feet wouldn’t move at all.

lines.japanese: 目の前に霞がかかる。おかしいな、ここはどこだろう。だんだんと視界だけじゃなく、頭の中にも靄がかかり、やがて――
lines.english: A haze spread before my eyes. How strange. Where was I? Mist gathered not only over my vision but inside my head, thickening until at last—

lines.japanese: 「こらー、ネクタイ汚すなー」
lines.english: “Hey! Don't get that all over your tie.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: ふいに意識を現実に引きもどされた。あれ？　たったいま僕は、グレタガルドに旅立とうとしてたような……。
lines.english: My consciousness was abruptly hauled back into reality. Huh? A moment ago, hadn't I been on the verge of departing for Gretagard...?

lines.japanese: だけど目の前にいるのは、明らかにこっちの世界の住人だった。
lines.english: But the person before me was unmistakably a resident of this world.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、食べたものが飛び散ってる」
lines.english: “Look. You've spat food all over it.”

lines.japanese: そのままぼうっと突ったっていたら、彼女の腕が伸びてきたので慌てて手を振る。
lines.english: I remained standing there in a daze. When she reached toward me, I hurriedly waved her off.

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　い、いいよ」
lines.english: “What? N-no, it's fine.”

lines.japanese: 「良くないでしょ。ほらそのままでいいから」
lines.english: “It isn't fine. Here, hold still.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だってみんな見てるし」
lines.english: “But everyone's looking.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはハンカチで僕のネクタイの汚れを拭き、そのあと……。
lines.english: Watarai wiped the stain from my tie with her handkerchief. Then...

lines.japanese: 「ほら、緩んでる」
lines.english: “See? It's loose.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ネクタイを上下でつかまえてきゅっとしぼった。
lines.english: She took the tie above and below the knot and pulled it snug.

lines.japanese: 「服装の乱れは心の乱れ。付けいる隙を見せないようにしないとね」
lines.english: “A disorderly appearance betrays a disorderly heart. You mustn’t show anyone an opening.”
“Oh. Right...”

lines.japanese: 「ちゃんとしなくちゃ」
lines.english: “Gotta make you presentable.”

lines.japanese: 僕の胸元で渡来さんの両手にきゅっと力がこもる。少しきついくらいだけど、喉元以上に気持ちが締まった。彼女から距離を詰められるとどうしてこんなに胸が脈打つんだろう。
lines.english: Watarai's hands tightened at my chest. The tie was a little too tight, but it did even more to make me pull myself together. Why did my heart beat so violently whenever she drew close?

lines.japanese: 彼女の前髪が少し鼻先を掠める。柔らかい感触がして、グレタガルドの妖精たちよりもフローラルな香りが漂ってきた。
lines.english: Her bangs brushed the tip of my nose. They were soft, and she carried a fragrance more floral than any fairy of Gretagard.

lines.japanese: 「昨日だって言われてるんだから、羽田君がしっかりしないと」
lines.english: “After what you were told yesterday, Haneda, you really do need to get it together.”

lines.japanese: 「昨日？」
lines.english: “Yesterday?”

lines.japanese: 「そっか……昨日のこと覚えてないんだ」
lines.english: “Oh... You don't remember yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 彼女の手の力が「きゅっ」から「ぎゅっ」に変わった。
lines.english: The pressure of her hands went from a little “tug” to a hard “yank.”

lines.japanese: 「く、苦しいよ渡来ざん」
lines.english: “W-Wadarai, I can't breathe.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめん」
lines.english: “Oh. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、高内さんに迷惑をかけたのは覚えてるんだけど……」
lines.english: “Um, I remember causing trouble for Takauchi...”

lines.japanese: 「や、理不尽なこと言われたのは羽田君じゃん」
lines.english: “But you were the one she was treating completely unfairly.”

lines.japanese: 「それはおれが時間を間違えたからで、高内さんは悪くないんだ」
lines.english: “Only because I got the time wrong. Takauchi didn't do anything wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう」
lines.english: “Oh?”

lines.japanese: ただでさえ大きな渡来さんの目が丸くなる。僕のネクタイを握っている彼女の手から、力が抜けていった。
lines.english: Watarai's already large eyes grew round. The strength drained from the hand clutching my tie.

lines.japanese: 「もし悲しいことを悲しいと認識しないで生きていけるとしたら、それは幸福なことなのかな」
lines.english: “If a person could live without recognizing sorrow as sorrow, would that make them happy?”

lines.japanese: 「え、それって誰のこと？」
lines.english: “What? Who are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん」
lines.english: “No one.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはにっこりと笑った。僕にはそれ以上彼女の顔を見続ける度胸がなかった。
lines.english: Watarai smiled. I didn’t have the nerve to keep looking at her.

lines.japanese: 「どこか行くところだったの？」
lines.english: “Were you going somewhere?”

lines.japanese: 僕が目を逸らすと、彼女の手が重力のままにするりと落ちていった。
lines.english: When I looked away, her hand slid smoothly down as gravity took it.

lines.japanese: 「え？　どこか？」
lines.english: “What? Somewhere?”

lines.japanese: 「お財布持って立ち上がったから」
lines.english: “You stood up holding your wallet.”

lines.japanese: あ、そうだ。僕は飲み物を買いにいこうとしていたんだ。でも高内さんはすでに昼食は終えているみたいだし、その必要もなさそうだ。
lines.english: Oh, right. I had been going to buy something to drink. But Takauchi seemed to have finished her lunch already, so there was probably no need anymore.

lines.japanese: 「いや別に。食べおわったから立ちあがっただけだよ」
lines.english: “No, nowhere. I only stood up because I'd finished eating.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……いつもパン食なんだ？」
lines.english: “Hmm... Do you always eat bread for lunch?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、そんなカンジかな」
lines.english: “Yes. More or less.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはパンの空き袋を見ると、ちょっと首を傾げた。なんていうか可憐だ。
lines.english: Watarai looked at the empty bread bags and tilted her head a little. I don’t know how to put it. She looked lovely.

lines.japanese: 「……やり過ぎかな」
lines.english: “...Maybe I'm overdoing it.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はそのポーズをとったまま、すたすたと僕の席から離れていった。
lines.english: Still holding that pose, she marched briskly away from my desk.

lines.japanese: なんだったんだろう。
lines.english: What had that been about?

lines.japanese: 取り残された僕は次にするべき行動を考えてみた。そうだ、昼休み残りの時間で針生さんに声をかけてみよう。
lines.english: Left by myself, I thought about what to do next. Right. I’d try talking to Hariu with the rest of lunch.

lines.japanese: 羽田班に編成されるのは形だけ、と彼は言ったけど、もしかして僕からきちんとお願いすれば協力してもらえるかもしれない。
lines.english: He’d said he was only joining the Haneda group on paper, but maybe he’d actually help if I asked him properly myself.

lines.japanese: 自分の席で億劫そうにまぶたを閉じている針生さんは、今にも教室の外へ行ってしまいそうだ。僕は急ぎ足で彼の席に向かった。
lines.english: Hariu had closed his eyes at his desk like even that was a bother, and looked ready to leave the classroom any second. I hurried toward him.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん」
lines.english: “Hariu.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 返事はあったけど、針生さんの目は僕の方へ向かなかった。左右に小さく揺れながら、相変わらず視線が落ちつかない。
lines.english: He answered, but did not turn his eyes to me. They continued their restless little drift from side to side.

lines.japanese: 「あの、さっきの会議で決まった件なんですけど」
lines.english: “Um, it's about what we decided in the meeting just now.”

lines.japanese: 話しかけはしたけど、何を言えばいいのか分からなかった。針生さんも一言発しただけで、言葉を続けようとはしない。
lines.english: I’d started talking to him, but had no idea what to say. Hariu had only said one word and wasn’t trying to keep the conversation going either.

lines.japanese: 正直言って話しかけたのをちょっと後悔したけど、いまは前に進むべきだ。
lines.english: Honestly, I kind of regretted talking to him, but I had to keep going now.

lines.japanese: 「えっと、もし空いてる日があれば、一日でも参加してもらえないかと思ったんです」
lines.english: “If you have a free day, I was wondering whether you might join us. Even for just one day.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、そんな学校ごっこに興味はない。まあ、やるなら健全な――ハハ、健全だって。おまえとその仲間たちでやってくれ。これでも忙しい身なんだ」
lines.english: “Ha. I’ve no interest in playing schoolchildren. If you’re determined to indulge in something so wholesome—ha! Wholesome—then you and your little friends can manage it. I am a busy man, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「仲間って言っても、渡来さんと……あとは山科さんも来てないし……」
lines.english: “Friends... There's Watarai, but... Yamashina isn't here either...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはもう一度首を右に傾けた。
lines.english: Hariu tipped his head to the right once more.

lines.japanese: 「そうか、明日香も同じ班だったなァ。なるほどなるほど、面白そうな話ではあるけど、俺とおまえと、明日香かァ……」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Asuka is in the same group, isn't she? I see, I see. That does make it sound rather more interesting. You, Asuka, and me...”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは眼鏡のブリッジを押さえながら、独り言みたいに呟いた。渡来さんの名前に反応したぐらいだから、やっぱり彼女とは仲がいいんだろう。
lines.english: Hariu pressed the bridge of his glasses and muttered like he was talking to himself. He’d reacted to Watarai’s name, so they probably really were close.

lines.japanese: だけど、いまの僕はなんとか彼に協力してもらおうと必死だった。渡来さんの名前を出せば、針生さんが協力してくれるかもしれない。
lines.english: But right then I was desperate to get him to help somehow. Maybe bringing up Watarai would do it.

lines.japanese: 「そうなんです。渡来さん同じ班だし、針生さんは彼女と友達みたいだから、一緒に作業をしてもらえないかと思ったんです」
lines.english: “That's right. Watarai is in our group, and you seem to be friends with her, so I thought perhaps you could work with us.”

lines.japanese: 「ふン」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは小さく頭を落とした。それが了の返事に見えて、僕は一歩踏みだしかけた。
lines.english: Hariu dipped his head. It looked like assent, and I nearly stepped forward.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、手伝ってくれるんですか？」
lines.english: “You'll help us?”

lines.japanese: 「いや」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはゆっくりとした動作で右手を突きだした。
lines.english: Hariu slowly extended his right hand.

lines.japanese: 「いや今日はなァ、切符を買いに行きたいんだ」
lines.english: “No, today I need to go buy a ticket.”

lines.japanese: 「切符？　えっ……どこか旅行に行くんですか？」
lines.english: “A ticket? Are you... going on a trip somewhere?”

lines.japanese: 「そんなこと、なんでおまえに教えなきゃいけないの」
lines.english: “Why should I have to tell you that?”

lines.japanese: 「あんまり遠出したことはないんですけど、おれも旅行って好きなんです」
lines.english: “I haven't traveled very far myself, but I like traveling too.”

lines.japanese: 「遠出したことないのに、旅行が好き？」
lines.english: “You like traveling, even though you've never been far from home?”

lines.japanese: 「旅行記の写真なんて、見てるだけで楽しいですよね。針生さんはどこに行くんですか？　おれは野鳥の観察なんかしたいんですけど――」
lines.english: “Even looking at photographs in travel books is fun, don't you think? Where are you going? I'd like to go birdwatching somewhere—”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なんですか？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: それまでふらついていた視線が急に僕を捕えた。
lines.english: His wandering eyes suddenly locked onto me.

lines.japanese: 「へえー、俺は……」
lines.english: “Well, I...”

lines.japanese: 「ダム」
lines.english: “Dams.”

lines.japanese: 「ダム？　え、ダムってあの水を堰きとめるダムですか？」
lines.english: “Dams? You mean the kind that hold back water?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえダム好きか」
lines.english: “You like dams?”

lines.japanese: 「ダムですか」
lines.english: “Dams?”

lines.japanese: 「そう、ダム」
lines.english: “Yes. Dams.”

lines.japanese: 「ダムだ。いいよなあ、ダム。なんかほっとするだろ。放流なんかしてたらおまえ、どうする。どうせなら、週末に台風でも来ねえかなあ。それか、空っからになって貯水量ゼロもいいよなあ」
lines.english: “Dams. Dams are great. Something relaxing about them, right? What if they were releasing water, huh? What’d you do then? Maybe we’ll get a typhoon this weekend. Or hey, bone-dry with the reservoir at zero—that’d be good too.”

lines.japanese: 「すみません、ちょっとおれには分かりません」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I don't think I understand.”

lines.japanese: 「謝る必要はないだろ。関心がないことに他の人間が干渉するべきじゃない。その代わり、俺の趣味にも干渉するな。悪いけど日曜日の打ち合わせがあるんで帰らせてもらう」
lines.english: “No need to apologize. Other people shouldn’t interfere with what someone isn’t interested in. So don’t interfere with my hobbies either. Sorry, but I’ve got a meeting about Sunday, so I’m leaving.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあまた今度……」
lines.english: “Maybe next time…”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、おまえもたまにはダムって来いよ」
lines.english: “Sure. You ought to go damming sometime yourself.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは５００ミリペットを取り出すと、ごくりと喉に通す音を立てた。
lines.english: Hariu took out his half-liter bottle and swallowed with an audible gulp.

lines.japanese: 僕は彼が教室から立ちさるまで、座席の横でただ突ったっていた。
lines.english: I simply stood beside his desk until he had left the classroom.

lines.japanese: ケータイのメモ帳を開いて残務処理の一つを確かめる。
lines.english: I opened the notes on my phone and reviewed one item of unfinished business.

lines.japanese: “６：クラスに友達をつくる”
lines.english: “6. Make a friend in class.”

lines.japanese: 僕はいま何を思ったんだろう。
lines.english: What had I been thinking just now?

lines.japanese: それが針生さんに対してのものだと思ったら、なんだか可笑しくて仕方なかった。
lines.english: Thinking it had been aimed at Hariu was so funny I couldn’t help it.

lines.japanese: 帰りのＨＲも終わり、級友たちがそれぞれ放課後の過ごし方なんかについて語らいはじめた。
lines.english: Afternoon homeroom ended, and my classmates began discussing their various plans for after school.

lines.japanese: やがて清掃担当を残して、一人、また一人と教室から姿を消してゆく。
lines.english: Before long, leaving only the students on cleaning duty, they vanished from the classroom one by one.

lines.japanese: そして最後の一人が用具入れにほうきを入れて、後ろのドアから出てゆくのを見届けたあと、僕は机の上にきのう渡されたルーズリーフのリフィルを広げた。
lines.english: After I watched the last person put a broom in the supply closet and leave through the back door, I spread the loose-leaf sheet from yesterday on my desk.

lines.japanese: 改めて見ても片務的な作業内容。今日の会議でさらに作業が増えたせいで、ほとんどが僕の班に押しつけられていた。
lines.english: Even at a second look, the arrangement was painfully one-sided. Today's meeting had added still more work, and nearly all of it had been foisted upon my group.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いたいた」
lines.english: “Ah, there you are.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: しばらくぼうっと机に体を倒していると、前のドアから長い髪が顔を覗かせる。僕は慌てて作業書をしまいこんだ。
lines.english: I had been lying slackly over my desk for some time when a curtain of long hair peeked around the front door. I hurriedly put the work sheet away.

lines.japanese: 「落ちこんでるかなーと思って見にきたよ」
lines.english: “I thought you might be feeling down, so I came to check on you.”

lines.japanese: 「落ちこんでなんかないよ」
lines.english: “I'm not feeling down.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、なんで今ぐたってしてたの」
lines.english: “Then why were you slumped over your desk just now?”

lines.japanese: 「してないよ。失礼なこと言わないでよ」
lines.english: “I wasn't. Don't say such rude things.”

lines.japanese: 良かった、例のメモは見られなかったみたいだ。一方的な作業内容なんかはいいけど、その下段に書かれた落書きだけは彼女に見られたくなかった。
lines.english: Good. It looked like she hadn’t seen that note. I didn’t care about the one-sided list of work and stuff, but I definitely didn’t want her seeing the scribble at the bottom.

lines.japanese: 「まったく、こうして甲斐甲斐しく様子を見にきた恋人に向かって、ひどいよね」
lines.english: “Honestly. What a cruel thing to say to the devoted girlfriend who came all this way to check on you.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なんのこと？」
lines.english: “Huh? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「それ」
lines.english: “That.”

lines.japanese: 彼女が指差した先には僕の鞄があった。なんだ、やっぱり見られちゃったのか。
lines.english: She was pointing at my bag. So she had seen it after all.

lines.japanese: “明日香様とイチャつく”
lines.english: “Flirt with Lady Asuka.”

lines.japanese: それは高内さんたちが冷やかしで書いた一文だ。僕だけならともかく、仮の恋人である彼女にまで迷惑がかかることが居たたまれなかった。
lines.english: Takauchi and the others had written it to tease me. It was one thing if I was the only one, but I couldn’t stand their causing trouble for the girl who was only pretending to be my girlfriend too.

lines.japanese: 「どれ、ちょいと見せて」
lines.english: “Here, let me have a look.”

lines.japanese: 「え、やだよ」
lines.english: “What? No.”

lines.japanese: 「いいから見せてよう」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. Let me see.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは笑顔だったけど、有無を言わさぬ迫力でそれを奪いとった。机の真ん中に広げる。
lines.english: Watarai was smiling, but the force behind that smile permitted no refusal. She snatched the page away and spread it across the middle of the desk.

lines.japanese: 「うわー、これはなかなかの量だよね」
lines.english: “Wow, that’s quite a lot, huh?”
“What is?”

lines.japanese: 「私たちのお仕事」
lines.english: “All our work.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが示した箇所は下段の落書きじゃなく、作業指示の部分だった。ひぃふぅみぃと指で数えている。
lines.english: Watarai was pointing at the work instructions, not the scribble underneath. ‘One, two, three...’ she counted on her fingers in a little singsong.

lines.japanese: 「なるほど、これは羽田班一同の奮闘が期待されるわけだね」
lines.english: “I see. Great feats of valor will be expected from every member of the Haneda group.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でも、おれの仕事をみんなに手伝わせるわけにはいかないよ」
lines.english: “But I can't make everyone else help with my work.”

lines.japanese: 「なに言ってんの。一人でやるより二人でやった方がいいでしょ」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? Two people are better than one.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は僕の肩にぽんと手を置いた。
lines.english: She placed a hand lightly on my shoulder.

lines.japanese: 触れられた箇所から温かさが広がるみたいだ。そういえば前に誰かが言ってた。渡来さんからは、精神活動を活性化させるなにかが出てるんじゃないかって。
lines.english: Warmth seemed to spread out from where she touched me. Come to think of it, someone once said Watarai might give off something that gets your brain going.

lines.japanese: 「うん。そうだね、みんなでやった方が早い……かな」
lines.english: “Yes. You're right. It will go faster if we all do it together... probably.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、力を合わせて終わらせちゃおう」
lines.english: “Exactly. We'll join forces and knock it out.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「よーし、羽田班しまっていこーッ」
lines.english: “All right! Haneda group, let’s get to work!”

lines.japanese: 僕の肩を離陸した白い手が、握りこぶしとなって高々突きあげられた。
lines.english: The white hand took flight from my shoulder, curled into a fist, and rose triumphantly overhead.

lines.japanese: 「彼女だしね？」
lines.english: “I am your girlfriend, after all.”

lines.japanese: そして紙面の下方、あの他愛もない落書きの内容を指ししめす。
lines.english: Then she pointed farther down the page, at that foolish little scrawl.

lines.japanese: 僕が気を重くした一文も、彼女に笑ってもらえれば途端に活力へ変わる気がした。
lines.english: Even the one sentence that had weighed on me felt like it could turn into energy the moment she laughed at it.

lines.japanese: 「んー、それにしても、好き勝手書いてくれちゃってまあ」
lines.english: “Hmm… Still, they sure wrote whatever they felt like.”

lines.japanese: 紙面の落書きでは、際立つ特徴を持った同級生たちが無責任に揶揄されている。針生さんや山科さんを想起させえるものもあった。
lines.english: The scribbles irresponsibly mocked classmates whose peculiarities made them easy targets. Some clearly evoked Hariu and Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 「針生先輩は別にいいけど、山科にこれは見せられないよね。うん、こういうおふざけが過ぎるのはちょっと」
lines.english: “Hariu's one thing, but we can't let Yamashina see this. Yeah, this joke goes a little too far.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは別にいいんだ。
lines.english: So it did not matter when it was Hariu.

lines.japanese: 僕は嫌だな。針生さんでも山科さんでも、こんなふうに言われてるのは。
lines.english: I don't like it. Whether it's Hariu or Yamashina, I don't like hearing people talk about them that way.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんは山科さんと仲がいいの？」
lines.english: “Are you close with Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　んー……どうだろう。フツーに話すけど、フツーにクラスメイトだよね」
lines.english: “Hm? Well... I don't know. We talk normally, but we're just regular classmates.”

lines.japanese: 「フツーって？」
lines.english: “What do you mean by normally?”

lines.japanese: 「普通のクラスメイト。羽田君にとっての普通のクラスメイトと同じだと思うよ」
lines.english: “A normal classmate. I imagine she's the same as any normal classmate is to you.”

lines.japanese: つまり、事務的会話以上、帰りのお誘い未満。なるほど、フツーに普通のクラスメイトだ。
lines.english: So: more than business-only talk, less than asking her to walk home. Got it. A perfectly normal, ordinary classmate.

lines.japanese: 「なるほど……うん、なるほど」
lines.english: “I see... Yes. I see.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why do you ask?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　いや、だって山科さん同じ班だから、おれもどんなひとなのか知っておきたいし」
lines.english: “What? Oh, because Yamashina is in our group. I thought I should know what sort of person she is.”

lines.japanese: 「山科に興味あるんだ」
lines.english: “So you're interested in Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なんで？」
lines.english: “What? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「だって羽田君が他人のこと聞いてくるなんて珍しいよね」
lines.english: “Because it's rare for you to ask about anyone else.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　そうかな、べつに普通だと思うけど」
lines.english: “It is? I think it's perfectly normal.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なに。普通だよ。いいでしょ、おれ班長なんだから、同じ班のひとに興味持ったって。普通だよ」
lines.english: “W-what? It's normal. I'm allowed to be interested in the people in my group. I'm the group leader. It's perfectly normal.”

lines.japanese: 「ふううーん」
lines.english: “Hmmm.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、ほらもう、遊んでないで渡来さん。手伝ってくれるなら早く分担決めちゃおうよ。さっきから話してばっかりで、ぜんぜん進んでないじゃない」
lines.english: “Oh, come on, Watarai, stop playing around. If you're going to help, let's divide up the work. We've done nothing but talk, and we haven't made any progress at all.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、それって私のせいなの？　せっかく元気づけに来た彼女に向かってなんだと」
lines.english: “What? And that's my fault? Is that any way to speak to the girlfriend who came here especially to cheer you up?”

lines.japanese: 「いいから、はいこれ。まず渡来さんには写真調達やってもらうから、準備しておいて」
lines.english: “Never mind that. Here. First, you’ll handle getting the photos, so be ready.”

lines.japanese: 僕は作業書を手にとって渡来さんの鼻先へ突きつけた。紙一枚の向こうで不服のうめきと、次いでそれを打ち消す笑い声が起こった。
lines.english: I picked up the work sheet and shoved it under Watarai's nose. From behind that one sheet came a groan of protest, then a laugh that canceled it out.

lines.japanese: 釣りこまれて僕もあははと笑った。彼女が笑いおえるまで僕も笑いつづけた。さっきまで静かだった教室が、まるで休み時間みたいに明るく華やいだ。
lines.english: Her laughter drew mine out with it. I went on laughing until she stopped. The classroom, silent only moments ago, grew bright and festive, as though it were break time.

lines.japanese: 「さて、じゃあ作業は明日からだし、今日はそろそろ帰るね」
lines.english: “Well, the work starts tomorrow, so I think I'll head home for today.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は一息つくと、鞄を握りなおして背中を向けた。
lines.english: She took a breath, adjusted her grip on her bag, and turned her back.

lines.japanese: 「あ。渡来さん！」
lines.english: “Wait. Watarai!”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は半回転させた体を、そのままの方向にくるりともう半回転させて戻ってきた。面白い動きをするひとだ。
lines.english: She'd turned halfway around, then twirled the rest of the way in the same direction until she was facing me again. She moved in funny ways.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ええと……」
lines.english: “Oh, um...”

lines.japanese: 思わず呼びとめはしたものの、なんで自分でも声をかけたのかよく分からなかった。なんだろう。たぶん心残りがあったんだ。
lines.english: I called after her without thinking, though I couldn't really say why. What was it? Maybe something was still bothering me.

lines.japanese: “君ね、誘いたいなら誘いなさい”
lines.english: “Listen. If you want to invite someone, then invite them.”

lines.japanese: きのう彼女に言われた言葉を思いだした。もしかして僕は、そんな大それた目的で呼びとめたんだろうか。当たり前だ、他に理由がない。
lines.english: I remembered what she'd told me yesterday. Had I really stopped her for something that grand? Of course. What else could it be?

lines.japanese: でも断られたらどうしよう。格好悪いかな。僕は上手く笑えるかな。渡来さんのことが好きだって気付かれないかな。その後ぎくしゃくしないかな。話しかけてもらえなくなっちゃうかな。
lines.english: But what if she refused? Would I look pathetic? Would I manage to smile? Would she realize I liked her? Would things be awkward afterward? Would she stop speaking to me altogether?

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは鞄を後ろ手に、上半身をぶらぶらさせて待っている。
lines.english: Watarai waited with her bag held behind her, idly swaying from the waist.

lines.japanese: 「どした？」
lines.english: “What's up?”

lines.japanese: 迷ってる場合じゃない。うじうじ考えないで、さらっと告げてしまおう。そうだ、たしか彼女は、男らしく当たって砕けろとも言っていたじゃないか。
lines.english: No time to hesitate. Quit brooding and just come out with it. Right—hadn't she told me to be a man and take my shot, even if I crashed and burned?

lines.japanese: 「一緒に帰っていいかな」
lines.english: “Would it be all right if I walked home with you?”

lines.japanese: 口にした瞬間、顔が燃えあがるようだった。だけど男らしさってやつを誇示したくて、僕はつとめて平静を装った。
lines.english: The moment I said it, my face felt like it caught fire. But I wanted to show off how manly I was, so I tried my best to look calm.

lines.japanese: 「あの、まあ、きのう言ってた、その、ゲームショップとか……うん、付きあうし……」
lines.english: “I mean, um, that game shop you mentioned yesterday... I could go with you...”

lines.japanese: 言葉を濁しながら返事を待つ、長いのか短いのかわけの分からない時間。
lines.english: I let the words trail off and waited. I had no idea if it was a long time or a short one.

lines.japanese: やがて渡来さんは右の方へふら～と傾きながら、そのまま風に吹かれるように教室の端まで流されていった。
lines.english: After a while, Watarai leaned waaay over to the right and drifted all the way to the edge of the classroom like the wind was carrying her.

lines.japanese: そして壁まで辿りつくと、ふたたび「あ～」と同じ声をあげながら戻ってきた。
lines.english: Upon reaching the wall, she raised the same long “ahh” and came drifting back.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん。今日は砕けて」
lines.english: “I’m sorry. Today, you crash and burn.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、分かった」
lines.english: “Okay.”

lines.japanese: 僕はにっこり笑った。わりとショックなのに、思ったより冷静でいられることは、自分でも意外だった。
lines.english: I smiled. The refusal had struck a fairly serious blow, so even I was surprised by how calm I felt.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんね、ほんとごめん」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I'm really, really sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「いや大丈夫だよ、男の子だから」
lines.english: “It's all right. I'm a boy. I can take it.”

lines.japanese: 「いまも待たせちゃってるんだ」
lines.english: “I'm keeping them waiting even now.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは教室の外を指差した。ドアの向こう、ふたつの人影がときおり教室の中を覗いていることに今さら気がついた。
lines.english: Watarai pointed outside the classroom. Only then did I notice the two figures beyond the door, peeking in from time to time.

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ、また明日ね」
lines.english: “All right. Then I'll see you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「動揺してない」
lines.english: “You aren't shaken.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「砕けたというのに、まるで動揺が見られない」
lines.english: “You crashed and burned, but you don't look shaken at all.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。これでもガツーンときたんだよ」
lines.english: “That’s not true. It hit me hard.”

lines.japanese: 「うっ……ごめん、ほんとにごめん」
lines.english: “Oh... I'm sorry. I'm really sorry.”

lines.japanese: どっちにしろすっきりしないんだ。難しい性格なんだな。
lines.english: Either way, it wouldn't sit right with her. She's complicated.

lines.japanese: 「これは貸しイチってことで」
lines.english: “Then let's say I owe you one.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、いいよ。きのうはおれがドタキャンしたから、これで貸し借りなしだ」
lines.english: “Ahaha, don't worry about it. I canceled on you at the last minute yesterday, so now we're even.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……」
まだ気にしてる。もしかしたら僕は、そんなに罪悪感を与えてしまうほど悲壮な顔でもしてるのだろうか。
lines.english: She was still worried about it. Did I look so tragic that I was making her feel that guilty?

lines.japanese: 「えっと、できればこれに懲りず……」
lines.english: “Well... I hope this won't put you off asking again...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、また今度一緒になったら帰ろう」
lines.english: “Yeah. Next time we get the chance, let's walk home together.”

lines.japanese: 「だねっ」
lines.english: “Yeah!”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはにこやかに手を振ると、教室のドアまで右に傾きながら流されていった。あれはまさか、彼女なりに残念だったことを表してくれてるのかな。
lines.english: Watarai waved brightly, then drifted toward the classroom door while listing to the right. Could that have been her own way of showing that she was disappointed too?

lines.japanese: そんなわけないか。どうせ社交的な渡来さんの、よくあるクラスメイトへの気遣いだろう。
lines.english: Of course not. Sociable Watarai must show that sort of consideration to classmates all the time.

lines.japanese: でも、ちょっとは残念だと思ってくれたのかな。僕が絞りだした勇気の十分の一くらいには。
lines.english: Still, perhaps she had been a little disappointed. A tenth as disappointed, say, as the courage I had wrung out of myself.
